characterization_methods.key_findings: Provides the initial mixed-grain PAG microstructure (Fig 4a) and PAG size data used for DRX/AGS determination.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens split along axial direction; sections ground with SiC papers, polished with 1 µm and 0.25 µm diamond pastes, chemically etched with saturated picric acid solution; Image Pro Plus software used for equivalent PAG diameter.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe prior austenite grain (PAG) structure at the center of the side section and calculate the equivalent diameter of each PAG.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SU5000 scanning electron microscope equipped with an EBSD detector
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD samples electrolytically polished with 10% perchlorate alcohol solution at 30 V and 0.25 A for 30 s after grinding and mechanical polishing; EBSD step size 0.65–1.3 µm.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the as-quenched martensitic microstructure and reconstruct prior austenite grains.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ARPGE software (Greninger-Troiano orientation relationship); AZtecCrystal software (GOS threshold 3°)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the constant 950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ condition at 0.9 strain: AGS 52.01±3.48 µm, DRX fraction 97.2%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: GOS threshold defined at 3°; equivalent PAG diameter calculated from reconstructed EBSD IPF maps considering boundaries with misorientation angles higher than 10°.
characterization_methods.purpose: Reconstruct prior austenite grains from as-quenched martensite EBSD maps and distinguish recrystallized grains from deformed ones.
characterization_methods.technique: EBSD data post-processing (PAG reconstruction and GOS analysis)

analytical_models.equation_role: Calibrates characteristic stresses (σ0, σss, σs, σc) and DRX kinetics (t0.5, DRX fraction) used to drive CA dislocation accumulation/annihilation and nucleation
analytical_models.model_name: Modified phenomenological constitutive model (STG-based characteristic stresses and DRX kinetics)
analytical_models.model_note: Material parameters from Table 1, obtained by genetic algorithm optimization (Appendix A2).

analytical_models.equation_role: GBS strain rate, DRX nucleation, grain boundary energy/mobility, and dislocation-density–stress coupling parameters
analytical_models.model_note: Material parameters from Table 4; K, b, ν, δDob, nGB, Vm and αdis from literature; Cdrx, E, AGB, H0 and PGB solved by GA optimization (Appendix B1).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: RVE 550 µm × 550 µm × 550 µm; cell size L0 = 2.5 µm; initial uniform dislocation density 1×10^11 m^-2; constant deformation 950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ to true strain 0.9; characteristic stresses and DRX activation energy calibrated from the modified constitutive model (Section 3.1).
computational_details.simulation_method: 3D cellular automaton (CA) with inhomogeneous dislocation density and grain boundary sliding (GBS) for discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: At 0.9 strain: simulated AGS 52.52 µm vs experimental reconstructed AGS 52.01±3.48 µm; simulated DRX fraction 99.5% vs experimental 97.2%. At 0.5 strain: simulated AGS 60.70 µm (DRX 94.1%) vs experimental 56.97±5.24 µm. At 0.4 strain: simulated AGS 68.69 µm (DRX 76.9%).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Heated at 10 °C/s and held for 180 s to homogenize the austenite phase.

processing_steps.method: cooling to deformation temperature and holding
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooled to 950 °C at 10 °C/s and kept for 60 s to reduce temperature fluctuations before compression.

Constant-condition hot compression at 950 °C and effective strain rate 0.01 s⁻¹ to a final true strain (ε_total) of 0.9. Specimen: cylindrical ϕ6 mm × 9 mm cut along rolling direction; 0.1 mm tantalum foil placed between specimen ends and indenter to prevent interfacial melting and minimize friction.
Immediately water-quenched after deformation to freeze the high-temperature microstructure morphology.

measurement_conditions.environment: Gleeble 1500 thermomechanical simulator, uniaxial hot compression; 0.1 mm tantalum foil placed between specimen ends and indenter to minimize friction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Deformed to true strain 0.9; water-quenched after deformation
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical specimen ϕ6 mm × 9 mm, cut along rolling direction

stress_strain_curves: True stress–true strain hot-compression curve at 950 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹: stress rises to a peak just below 90 MPa (≈85 MPa) near true strain ≈0.2–0.3, then softens mildly to a minimum near 70 MPa.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Experimental metallographic (2D): AGS 141.66 µm, SD 54.54 µm, Min 10.22 µm, Max 265.20 µm; face d_ave = 166.00 µm (top), 131.59 µm (right), 127.63 µm (left).

microstructure_list.region: orthogonal sections (top/right/left faces, representative areas 550 µm × 550 µm)

structures.overall_structure: Initial mixed-grain austenite microstructure (as-homogenized prior austenite grains) before hot compression

center of side section (reconstructed prior austenite grains from EBSD)

structures.overall_structure: As-quenched martensitic microstructure after constant hot compression at 950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ to true strain 0.9; prior austenite grains reconstructed from EBSD show nearly complete recrystallization at 0.9 strain

unmapped_findings: DRX fraction vs time for the constant 950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ condition (Fig 6b): the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve completes the 0→1 transition, reaching DRX fraction 1.0 near 60–70 s.
This sample is the constant-condition reference (950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹) against which transiently varying strain-rate and temperature tests are compared in Figs 7–10, 13, 16 and 19–21.

The modified constitutive model's accuracy over constant deformation conditions (of which this sample is one) is reported in Table 2: flow stress RMSE 4.8944 MPa, R² 0.9909, AARE 3.91%; load RMSE 274.6820 N, R² 0.9918, AARE 6.65%.
